questions.q: Which sandbox type includes a complete copy of both metadata AND data, typically used for staging and final user acceptance testing?
options: Developer
Developer Pro
Partial Copy
Full
questions.explain: A Full sandbox is a complete copy of metadata and data, making it the right environment for realistic performance testing and final UAT before production.

questions.q: What does a change set actually move between two connected orgs?
options: Business records (rows of data) only
Metadata/configuration — objects, fields, rules, flows, layouts — never business data
User passwords and login credentials
Both metadata and business data equally
questions.explain: A change set is a configuration-deployment tool. It moves metadata components, not the actual records stored in the objects.

questions.q: An outbound change set includes a validation rule that references a brand-new custom field, but that field was not added to the change set. What is the practical consequence?
options: Salesforce automatically adds the missing field for you
The deployment will fail or be blocked during validation, because the dependency wasn't included
The validation rule deploys but is automatically deactivated
Nothing — fields and rules deploy completely independently
questions.explain: Change set components can have dependencies; a component that references something not included in the same change set (and not already present in the target org) causes a validation/deployment failure.

questions.q: What happens to an outbound change set once it has been uploaded to a target org?
options: It becomes closed, and its components can no longer be edited — you clone it to resend updated components
It is automatically deployed to production within 24 hours
It can still be freely edited and re-uploaded indefinitely
It is permanently deleted from the source org
questions.explain: After upload, a change set's status becomes closed. To send updated versions of its components, you create a clone of it.

questions.q: Why would a team move from change sets to Salesforce CLI (sf/sfdx) with the Metadata API instead?
options: Change sets are being fully removed from the platform
CLI deployments are always faster regardless of team size
The team needs version control, code review, CI/CD pipelines, or deployment to orgs outside the connected sandbox family — things change sets don't support
CLI deployments don't require any validation step
questions.explain: Change sets only move between already-connected orgs and have no built-in version control or CI/CD integration. CLI-based deployment from a version-controlled project is the standard replacement once a team needs those capabilities.
